| [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) v7 | Hilbert-space parts are extra data, not intrinsic | Carroll (2021), [LIT-123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md): a quantum theory is fixed up to unitary equivalence by the Hamiltonian's spectrum, and subsystems come from a factorisation that the dynamics must select. Van Rijsbergen ([LIT-262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)) computes only traces and inner products, and treats each observable's eigenbasis as a "point of view". DisCoCat's ε/η composition ([LIT-273](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md)) is orthogonally covariant, while its Frobenius sequel ([LIT-272](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)) stipulates a basis and composes by elementwise product in it. [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) is the same point for learned representations. This is a synthesis across the four, not a result any one of them states. It does not say that basis-dependent models are wrong; it says what they have assumed. | Active |
| [THEORY-020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-020.md) | KS obstruction lies in how contexts overlap | Stone (1936, 1937), [LIT-353](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md) and [LIT-358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-358.md): every Boolean ring is isomorphic to the compact open sets of its prime-ideal space, a totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff space that is compact exactly when there is a unit, and every such space arises this way. Kochen & Specker ([LIT-298](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-298.md), Thm 0) turn this into the criterion that a partial Boolean algebra embeds in a Boolean one iff its two-valued homomorphisms separate points. The joining of the two, that non-classicality needs more than one context, is the record's. Neither Stone paper uses "ultrafilter" or states a duality of categories. | Active |
| [THEORY-021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-021.md) v3 | Uniform superposition features form a POVM | Elhage et al. (2022), [LIT-323](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-323.md), found that features in uniform superposition settle into polytopes and tegum products, with feature dimensionalities clustering at 3/4, 2/3, 1/2, 2/5 and 3/8. The tight-frame and POVM reading is the reader's inference in [NOTE-278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-278.md), checked numerically there. It was refined when filing: a tegum product is not globally tight, but the Dᵢ-weighted POVM still sums to the identity. None of this is in the paper. It does not make superposition contextual or quantum, and it says nothing yet about trained real models. | Active |
| [THEORY-024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) v2 | Global sections restore classical Boolean logic | Ghose (2025), [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) — asserts that the Heyting algebra of truth values "becomes Boolean" when the presheaf data collapse to a global section, and that sheaves encode Boolean reasoning. Both claims are asserted, not proved. The record's readings refute them. The internal logic of a topos is fixed by the base category and its topology, not by whether one presheaf has a section (Isham–Butterfield, [LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md), §6). Sheaf toposes such as Sh(ℝ) are not Boolean ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)). The contextuality criterion itself is untouched. | Rejected |
| [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md) v3 | Topos quantum logic is Heyting, not orthomodular | Döring & Isham (2007, II), [LIT-335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md) — daseinisation maps each projector injectively to a clopen sub-object of the spectral presheaf, with δ(P∨Q) = δ(P)∨δ(Q) but only δ(P∧Q) ⪯ δ(P)∧δ(Q). The orthocomplement is carried to inner daseinisation, not to ¬δ(P). That Sub_cl(Σ) is Heyting (Thm 2.5) is sketched in the source, and the record re-derives it: each Σ_V is extremally disconnected, so Sub_cl(Σ) is a frame. Paper I ([LIT-343](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-343.md)) chooses intuitionistic deduction. Isham–Butterfield ([LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md)) state that the Heyting algebra is fixed by the base category. | Active |
| [THEORY-041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-041.md) | Quantum logic began modular, not orthomodular | Birkhoff & von Neumann (1936), [LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md) — the lattice of closed subspaces is orthocomplemented and not distributive. They propose modularity (L5), motivated by a dimension function, and give an explicit infinite-dimensional pentagon that breaks it. The word "orthomodular" does not occur. Husimi (1937), [LIT-357](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-357.md), derives modularity as the parallelogram law under a finite-chain assumption and uses the orthomodular identity as a step without naming it. Citing either paper for "the orthomodular lattice of quantum logic" misattributes it. | Active |
| [THEORY-042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-042.md) | Cross-sector superposition is operationally mixed | Wick, Wightman & Wigner (1952), [LIT-339](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-339.md) — they define a superselection rule and show that a superposition across sectors "is not a pure state, but a statistical mixture". They prove the rule from time reversal for integer versus half-integer angular momentum, and postulate it for charge with "no conclusive evidence". What follows for Birkhoff–von Neumann's lattice ([LIT-306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md)), a product of sector lattices with central sector projections, is the record's inference. The centre-of-the-algebra formulation belongs to Haag, who is not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-160.md) v3 | Bracket antisymmetry yields symmetry–conservation | Baez (2020), [LIT-819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-819.md), read in [NOTE-630](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-630.md), Theorems 3, 4, 8 and 10, with Alfsen and Shultz's theorem quoted as Theorem 12 and not checked here (QUESTION-142). With unique solutions to the flow equations, "a generates symmetries of b iff b generates symmetries of a" is {a, b} = 0 ⇔ {b, a} = 0. It assumes reversible one-parameter groups and an observable–generator map; it says nothing about dissipative or stochastic dynamics, nor about the Lagrangian form of Noether's theorem. | Active |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v5 | Causal structure is a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf, and on the space Θ₃ it is not a sheaf: two causal assignments on disjoint opens give one event two outputs on their common extension. That example was checked here, and it settles the claim. The source's Theorem 2.34, that the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event, is reported as the source's. Its proof was not read, and it is QUESTION-143. It does not say any physical or quantum data display the effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) v5 | Classical simulations never create contextuality | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md); Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2021, v2 2024), [LIT-845](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md). A simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Along any simulation the non-contextual fraction cannot fall; contextual models cannot be cloned; and which maps between model sets are classical non-adaptive procedures is a non-contextuality question on a hom scenario, re-derived here. No-signalling models only, and nothing about information preserved. | Active |
| [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) v3 | Noncontextuality no-go refutes Leibnizianity | Schmid, Selby and Spekkens (2020), [LIT-945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-945.md), §VI.C, §VIII (Eqs. 200, 214, 215), read in part in [NOTE-737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-737.md), which is Skimmed: §§II–IV and the proofs in Appendices C–G were not read. A Leibnizian classical realist representation implies a generalized-noncontextual one, so every noncontextuality no-go is a no-go for Leibnizian representations. The converse is Conjecture 1′, so a Leibnizianity failure is not shown to be a noncontextuality failure. The prepare-measure claim is stated, not derived, in the text read. | Active |
| [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md) v4 | Meet and join can't overextend concepts | Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), Theorem 9 and §§2.2–3.3, read in full in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md). The impossibility is a proof, and it needs only that membership is monotone in the subspace. The fits that place the k-type deviations in a tilted subspace lattice and the ∆-type ones in an emergent sector are models with free parameters, not tests. Negation appears only as the orthocomplement used to derive the conjunction model from the disjunction model; no negated concept is measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-309](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-309.md) v3 | Joint measurability alone trivializes KS | Budroni, Cabello, Gühne, Kleinmann & Larsson (2022), [LIT-263](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-263.md), §IV.B.2, Eqs. 27–28, adapting Fritz (2012), read in [NOTE-844](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-844.md). For a nonsignalling p(ab\|xy), the POVMs G^{xy}_{ab} = p(ab\|xy)𝟙 on a one-dimensional space are jointly measurable for each pair and reproduce p. So contextuality relative to joint measurability alone is trivial, and the review requires contexts of repeatable, nondisturbing measurements. Liang, Spekkens & Wiseman's sharpness parameter is the other known escape. | Active |
| [THEORY-315](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-315.md) v2 | Trade-off form can witness contextuality | Catani, Leifer, Scala, Schmid and Spekkens (2022), [LIT-980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-980.md), read in [NOTE-825](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-825.md). Proved analytically, with a saturating model, for preparation noncontextuality and exact operational equivalence. The bound constrains a whole uncertainty relation only in a theory where every state has the orbit; the qubit's circle violates it, and a classical theory without the symmetry escapes it. It needs no perfectly distinguishable states, and it is not a sheaf or Kochen–Specker criterion. | Active |
| [THEORY-403](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-403.md) | Classical toy field reproduces Mach–Zehnder | Catani, Leifer, Schmid & Spekkens (2021), [LIT-019](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-019.md), read in full in [NOTE-018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-018.md). Each mode carries a binary occupation and a binary phase; an agent may know at most one of N, Φ, N⊕Φ; the beamsplitter swaps N_L with Φ_L⊕Φ_R. The model gives the quantum statistics for the phase shifter, which-way detection, the bomb tester (¼), delayed choice and the eraser. The existence proof holds for that fragment. The paper's further claim, that the model is generalized-noncontextual and so classical by its preferred criterion, is asserted, not proved, and unbalanced beamsplitters already admit a no-go. | Active |
| [THEORY-416](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-416.md) | Quantum work has four inequivalent notions | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md). The review's one synthesis (§5.2, §7) sets four definitions side by side: ⟨W⟩ = ∫tr[ρḢ]dt (Eq. 2), W = E_m^(τ) − E_n^(0) (Eq. 24), A^ε ≈ −kT ln(Z_Λ*/Z) (Eq. 49) and w^max_ε = F^min_ε(ρ_S) − F(τ_S) (Eq. 50). Only the last two agree, and that agreement is an observation that two published formulas match, for states diagonal in energy. It is an informed judgement of a 2016 snapshot, not a theorem that the notions cannot be unified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-455](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-455.md) | Quantum formalism fits indivisible stochastics | Barandes (2023), [LIT-086](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-086.md), read in full in [NOTE-080](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-080.md). Γ_ij = \|Θ_ij\|² = tr(Θ†P_iΘP_j) is an identity (Θ_ij = √Γ_ij works), and a unitary Θ on the original space exists only for doubly stochastic Γ. Interference is the cross-term of Eq. 43 against a would-be Markov factorization, and a perfectly correlating environment that then evolves separately makes the process divisible (Eqs. 45–56). The "emergent" Schrödinger equation is the definition of H, unitarity is a choice the claimed gauge freedom does not preserve, and the decomposition is relative to a configuration basis the paper never fixes. | Active |
| [THEORY-459](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-459.md) | Exact duality excludes ontological emergence | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), §14.3, read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A formal argument from equinumerosity and surjectivity, strictly proven for finite sets, with an argument on physical grounds for the infinite case (fn. 57). Emergence here is novel reference in the domain of application, a semantic condition, not an information measure. AdS/CFT is the exception only to incompatibility with non-epistemic emergence, not to "not indicative": on a theoretically equivalent reading, its "emergent gravity" "cannot be understood as ontological emergence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-474](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-474.md) | Toy-bit ZX calculus mirrors stabilizer theory | Backens & Duman (2014), [LIT-054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-054.md), read in full in [NOTE-066](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-066.md). A red–green spider calculus interpreted in the category of relations is universal and sound, and complete by Backens' stabilizer route. A binary matrix is a valid toy state iff SᵀJS = 0, the stabilizer condition (Lemma 3). The phase-free rules coincide with stabilizer ZX. That the phase group is the only categorical difference is cited, not shown, and completeness leans on analogy for several steps. The paper does no ψ-epistemic analysis and says nothing about which operational difference the phase group carries. | Active |
| [THEORY-479](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-479.md) | Entropy is the unique information 1-cocycle | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md), read in [NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md). Theorems 1 and 3 are proved for finite spaces, through the Tverberg–Kendall–Lee result on measurable solutions of the fundamental equation of information. The hypotheses are stated three different ways in the paper; Theorem 1's is operative. The higher mutual informations appear as coboundaries, and Theorems B, D and F and the synergy reading are sketched or deferred to companion papers, so they are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-482](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-482.md) | Two-point work obeys classical fluctuation laws | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md), which reproduces the derivation (Eqs. 24–30). With W_{m,n} = E_m^(τ) − E_n^(0), a thermal start and closed unitary evolution, ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} follows from Σ_n p_{m\|n} = 1 (Eq. 29), identical in form to the classical relation. The identity is exact under its conditions. Its classicality is bought by the definition of work: two projective energy measurements destroy coherences, which is why the definition is contested. It says nothing about work defined without them. | Active |
| [THEORY-485](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md) | Wave-function realism leaves physics closed | Poltorak (2026), [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), an unrefereed preprint read in full in [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md). "Every physical effect has a sufficient physical cause" has two tacit parameters, a domain and a completeness relation. With the domain set to spacetime the principle fails under wave-function realism; with it set to the ontology of a complete fundamental theory it survives. The move to a breach needs a premise that wave-function realists deny. The conclusions are modest and close to analytic once the terms are defined. The target is conceded to be a picture, not a published argument, and the dynamical-to-causal bridge is asserted, not argued. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-513](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-513.md) | Prior-relative observational entropy unifies many | Schindler, Strasberg, Galke, Winter & Jabbour (2025), [LIT-082](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-082.md), read in full in [NOTE-043](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-043.md), with Proofs 1, 2, 7, 10 and 11 checked line by line. The bounds, the special cases and the decomposition are proved. The central target, a small divergence of the time-averaged state from the prior, is proved for no concrete system; in the paper's own examples "in none of those cases was the smallness proved here analytically" (p. 12). Unpublished as of the reading. | Active |
| [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) | Base category, not global sections, fixes logic | Butterfield & Isham (1998), [LIT-381](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-381.md), read in full in [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md): Theorem 4.1 proves that generalized FUNC is exactly naturality of ν : G → Ω, for any presheaf G of posets on any small category. In classical physics the value presheaf has a global section per microstate (3.6–3.7), yet the macrostate and microstate valuations are sieve-valued, and [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md) shows excluded middle failing at a microstate. Isham & Butterfield (1999), [LIT-389](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) ([NOTE-334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-334.md)), adds that Ω is unique for a given topos and that a base with one arrow between any two objects gives two-valued logic. The choice of base, and so of the logic, remains free. | Active |
| [THEORY-524](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-524.md) | Čech obstruction is exact on cyclic scenarios | Carù (2018), [LIT-280](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-280.md), read in [NOTE-253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-253.md), and the same result republished as Thm IV.32 of Carù's 2019 thesis, [LIT-281](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-281.md), read in [NOTE-254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-254.md). The cyclic theorem is proved and was confirmed on Hardy, on the (2,2,4) counterexample and on 659 random contextual cycle models. The failures beyond cycles (Prop 8.2 / IV.34, the §8 cover, Conjecture 9.1 / IV.41) are the readers' computations and a lifting lemma, not the author's. The joint models grow exponentially; nothing analyses the cost. | Active |
| [THEORY-526](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-526.md) v2 | Čech obstruction is sound but incomplete | Abramsky, Mansfield & Barbosa (2011), [LIT-277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md) ([NOTE-250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-250.md)); Abramsky, Barbosa, Kishida, Lal & Mansfield (2015), [LIT-278](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-278.md) ([NOTE-251](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-251.md)); Carù (2017), [LIT-279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-279.md) ([NOTE-252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-252.md)). The criterion (Prop 4.2 / Prop 16) and the All-vs-Nothing theorem (Thm 21) are proved; the three failures are explicit models, which the readers re-computed exactly over ℤ and ℤ/2. Two steps are the readers': that the §8 cover and the (2,2,4) model admit no All-vs-Nothing argument over any ring, by Thm 21 read contrapositively. The witness is possibilistic, so it cannot grade anything below strong contextuality. | Active |
| [THEORY-535](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-535.md) | Quasi-sets count indistinguishable particles | Holik, Jorge, Krause & Lombardi (2021), [LIT-107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md), read in full from the preprint in [NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md). The Lombardi–da Costa ontology of properties makes a quantum system a bundle of instances of universal type-properties, with no principle of individuality. Krause's quasi-set theory Q, reinterpreted over property-instances, represents an atomic bundle as a qset taking one instance from each qset of indiscernibles, guaranteed by Q's Axiom of Choice, and N particles as a subqset of quasi-cardinal N. The new formal content is about two pages (§6), the printed proofs contain errors, and states, actualization and dynamics are not formalized. The claims about Kochen–Specker and non-separability are recharacterizations by definition, not results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-545](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-545.md) | Quantum concept model is classical underneath | Aerts & Gabora (2005), Parts II and I, [LIT-312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-312.md) and [LIT-340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-340.md), read in [NOTE-299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-299.md) and [NOTE-294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-294.md). The structural facts are checks of the published model, not of the authors' prose: contexts are sums of basis projectors, counts are chosen to match rounded frequencies, and the authors call the result a "quantization" of a set-theoretical model. Part I's mark of non-classicality (eq. 19) is met by Boolean projection lattices too, and its lattice structure is supposed, not derived. The model as printed is also infeasible in two cells. It does not say that no quantum model of concepts does better. | Active |
| [THEORY-553](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-553.md) | Topos quantities take spread values, not reals | Döring & Isham, paper III (2007/8), [LIT-299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-299.md) ([NOTE-290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-290.md)), restated with additions in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). The Gel'fand transforms of daseinised operators grow as contexts shrink, so arrows into the constant presheaf ℝ are impossible (3.3–3.4). Each Â gives a natural transformation δ̆^o(A) : Σ → ℝ^⪰ (Thm 3.1), and Â ↦ δ̆^o(A) is injective, by de Groote's results. ℝ^⪰ is a monoid, not a group; differences need a group completion, whose global elements are the functions of bounded variation on the context poset. No choice among the candidate value objects is made, and the state-dependent reading of the spread is cited, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md) | KS contradictions refute measurement identity | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-836.md), read in full in [NOTE-623](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-623.md). The transitivity step is an elementary proof; the reading of the reductio is an argument that rests on it. It binds the random-variable representation only: the sheaf account keeps one variable per measurement and asks whether marginals glue, and a reader who holds that view is not bound by it. The paper also proves that a coupling of a binary connection is multimaximal iff adjacent pairs, ordered by their means, are maximally coupled (Theorem II.3). | Active |
| [THEORY-580](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-580.md) v2 | Causal explainability is a linear program | Gogioso and Pinzani (2023), [LIT-788](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-788.md), skimmed in [NOTE-624](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-624.md), with the proofs of the causaltope theorems (2.18, 2.19, 2.25) and of the lower bound (2.29) read and checked on promotion (2026-10-20), against the definitions they take from The Topology of Causality. The proofs are short because the work is in the definitions; the one step left implicit closes. The quantum switches witness indefinite order only relative to an ambient space with known no-signalling constraints, not absolutely. | Active |
| [THEORY-584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md) | Fidelity is minimized Bhattacharyya overlap | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md). min over POVMs of Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) equals tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28), attained in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67), whose eigenvalues are √(tr ρ0E_b / tr ρ1E_b) (Eq. 3.92). Proved for invertible ρ1 with a separate support construction, in finite dimension. The fidelity is the unsquared one; Jozsa's is its square. The thesis says nothing about trace distance, and the analogous problems for Rényi overlaps and the quantum Chernoff bound are left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-585.md) v3 | Topos pull-backs fail for tensor composites | Döring & Isham, paper IV (2007/8), [LIT-310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md) ([NOTE-285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-285.md)), restated in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) §§11–13 ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). Classical physics satisfies the translation condition (3.18) exactly. For quantum disjoint sums the pull-back of δ̆(A₁⊕A₂) is δ̆(A₁) (Lemma 4.2, 4.24; checked). For H₁⊗H₂ the pull-back gives δ(Â₁)_{V_W}⊗1̂ at each context W, which equals δ(Â₁⊗1̂)_W on contexts V₁⊗ℂ1̂. That it differs elsewhere, and that no operator realises it, are asserted. The rules are "partly experimental", and the trivial-system rule contradicts the series' own definition of contexts. | Active |
| [THEORY-586](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-586.md) | ψ-ontic states can still represent knowledge | Hance, Rarity & Ladyman (2021), [LIT-090](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-090.md), read in full in [NOTE-072](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-072.md). The formal ψ-ontic/ψ-epistemic split is contradictory by stipulation, while the informal "ontic" and "epistemic" are not exclusive. So PBR and the related theorems bound the geometry of µ_ψ, not the interpretation of ψ. The paper proves nothing; its positive criterion (Eq. 6) is predictive incompleteness, and its Appendix A makes claims the record's readings contradict. The defensible paraphrase of PBR is "not ψ-epistemic in the overlap sense, given preparation independence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-592](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-592.md) | C*-algebras embed as Hilbert-space operators | Gelfand & Naimark (1943), [LIT-313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-313.md), read in full in [NOTE-303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-303.md). Theorem 1 embeds every normed *-ring in B(H) for a Hilbert space not assumed separable; Lemma 1 is the commutative case, resting on Gelfand's 1941 paper and Šilov's boundary. The paper never says "C*-algebra" or "GNS". It assumes two axioms it suspected redundant, and notes that a single norm identity may replace two others. It gives the object-level isomorphism R ≅ C(𝔐), not a categorical duality, and nothing on uniqueness or irreducibility of the representation. | Active |
| [THEORY-594](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-594.md) | Inequivalent representations needn't sink OSR | French (2010 draft; SHPMP 2012), [LIT-170](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-170.md), read in [NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md) from the unpaginated preprint. Every technical step is imported (Wallace, Earman, Ruetsche, Halvorson & Müger, Baker); the paper's contribution is interpretive and informal. The DHR result that statistics and charge kinds follow from the algebra is strong physics; that it favours OSR is French's reading. The modal "trans-world" structure is proposed, not developed, and the combined third option "obviously requires further elaboration". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-605](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-605.md) | Preparation independence makes ψ ontic | Pusey, Barrett & Rudolph (2011), [LIT-062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-062.md), read in full in [NOTE-030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-030.md). For any two non-orthogonal pure states, n copies prepared independently and an entangled measurement in which each outcome is impossible for one product preparation force zero overlap; with ε error, D(µ0, µ1) ≥ 1 − 2ε^{1/n} (Eq. 7). Determinism and locality are not assumed. Preparation independence, in its strong product-space form, carries the weight, and dropping it permits ψ-epistemic models. The theorem excludes overlap, not every reading of ψ as knowledge, and it does not reach theories outside the ontological-models framework. | Active |
| [THEORY-619](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md) | Coarse-graining is direct image of clopens | Butterfield & Isham (2001), "Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: IV", [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md), read in full in [NOTE-328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-328.md). §2.4 proves G ≅ CloΣ: restricting the characters of V₁ that make P̂ true gives exactly the characters of V₂ that make its coarse-graining true, via a cited state-extension theorem. Theorem 3.1 shows that any assignment defined by "support ≤ coarse-grained proposition", with supports forming a global element of G, is a sieve-valued valuation obeying FUNC; a state's supports qualify. Both theorems are close to definitional. Nothing here builds Heyting operations on clopen sub-objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-621.md) | Relative facts resolve Wigner's friend | Rovelli (2021), [LIT-177](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-177.md), read in full in [NOTE-174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-174.md). For a fact a and exclusive facts bᵢ, the collapse rule Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and the unitary rule \|Σᵢ W(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² differ by interference; RQM applies the first only when the bᵢ and c are relative to the same system. Decoherence makes some relative facts stable. The core rule is postulated, not derived, and inter-observer consistency gets one sentence. The chapter is expository, and several of its headline claims outrun its support. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-630](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-630.md) | Protective measurement needn't show ψ ontic | Gao (2016), [LIT-121](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md), read in full in [NOTE-140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-140.md). Under Zeno protection the pointer shifts by exactly ⟨A⟩ with no entanglement (eqs. 1.9–1.13), and projectors on regions plus a current operator give ρ and j (eqs. 1.14–1.16). Gao argues three routes from this to ψ-ontology, claimed to need no preparation independence. All three rest on the premise that the protection does not "know" ψ, which Gao's own fn. 10 partly concedes is false. The random-discontinuous-motion ontology and the collapse model built on it are further, weaker steps. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-631.md) | Unitary and open QT can't be ranked neutrally | Cuffaro & Hartmann (2021), [LIT-037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-037.md), read in full in [NOTE-077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-077.md). Stinespring dilation one way and dropping Lindblad terms the other make the two frameworks a tie on ontic dependence (OntFund-1) and on justification (EpFund-1). The verdict for the open theory comes from OntFund-2, which holds only if orthodox and Everettian readings are all that count, and from EpFund-2, which rests on imperfect preparation. Explanatory fundamentality is effectively abandoned. The paper proves nothing formal, and its "tout court" conclusion outruns §4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-635](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-635.md) | Bohmian dispositions erase state differences | Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md), read in full in [NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md). Under the guidance law ψ(t) gives a vector field X_t on configuration space, read as a holistic disposition. For a particle in [0,1], each φn(x) = sin(πnx) gives zero velocity everywhere, so infinitely many energy eigenstates share one dispositional history, and the distinction between φ1 and φ2 in energy and typicality is lost. The rescue rests on Goldstein's unproved genericity conjecture (fn. 41), and the problem arises only for closed systems (fn. 42). It is a counterexample to one reading, not a verdict on ψ's category. | Active |
| [THEORY-656](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-656.md) | Holistic power can't ground effective ψ | Dorato (2015), [LIT-176](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-176.md), read in full in [NOTE-105](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-105.md). Against Esfeld et al.'s holistic dispositionalism: when a subsystem effectively decouples, its Hamiltonian's masses must be intrinsic dispositions of its particles, so the holistic view must alter its ontology between the universal and the effective wave function (pp. 14–15). The argument is moderate and posed partly as questions. The paper's wider thesis, that events are a common primitive ontology for GRW, Bohm and ψ-antirealist views, shows compatibility only, and Dorato concedes the difference from Esfeld could be verbal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-664](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-664.md) | Steering gives weak, not strong, self-duality | Barnum, Gaebler & Wilce (2009), [LIT-081](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-081.md), read in full in [NOTE-082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-082.md). A bipartite state steers its marginal iff its map on effects is a strong quotient of order intervals (Thm 5.4). With matching dimensions a steering state is an order-isomorphism, and a cone is homogeneous iff every interior state purifies to an isomorphism state (Thm 4.1). Hence universal self-steering gives homogeneity and weak self-duality (Prop. 5.8). The weaker Prop. 5.7 is thinly argued. The C*-algebraic conclusion of §6 needs strong self-duality, which the paper assumes rather than derives. | Active |
| [THEORY-669](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-669.md) | Nomological ψ pays in the theory of laws | Chen (2018), [LIT-204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-204.md) ([NOTE-175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md)), maps the realist readings and splits the nomological one into strong and weak. Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md) ([NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md)), ranks the costs of ψ-as-law: time-indexed laws are the serious obstacle, grades of necessity tolerable. Allori (2021), [LIT-200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md) ([NOTE-154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-154.md)), makes ψ an ingredient of the law, which may be time-dependent and non-unique, and so concedes Belot's point that ψ behaves like an initial condition. Each move is an informal argument. Chen reports, without endorsing, the objection that the weak reading is too cheap, and Allori's reply embraces the case it treats as a reductio. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-687.md) | Naive duals need metaphysics to pick a world | Le Bihan & Read (2018), [LIT-113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md), read in [NOTE-152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-152.md) from the accepted manuscript. A nontechnical survey whose central argument is informal. It assumes a duality relates empirically equivalent models (weaker than De Haro & Butterfield's isomorphism of a bare theory), that each model is read naively and internally, and that structuralism is set aside. Its reading said it supports no existing THEORY directly; this files the conditional verdict the survey argues for, and nothing more. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-690.md) | Dualities give no real underdetermination | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A case-by-case argument over the book's examples, with a logico-semantic fallback (each dual entails the common core) for a hypothetical genuine case. The rich-core verdict is argued from exact cases (bosonization, electric–magnetic duality, T-duality) and does not reach AdS/CFT or M-theory, where structural-realist readings were proposed and the common core is "partial … ongoing work in physics!". The commitment holds only where an interpreted common core exists, which the authors say is not true in general. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-695.md) | Broadcast iff commuting, clone iff orthogonal | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), §4.3, read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md), from the Barnum–Caves–Fuchs–Jozsa–Schumacher manuscript. Fidelity cannot decrease under partial trace or under the broadcasting map, so broadcasting forces equality conditions that make ρ0 commute with the optimal-fidelity operator. Proved for invertible ρ0, ρ1 only. Spekkens' epistricted classical theories ([LIT-007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md)) reproduce no-broadcasting, so the theorem states where broadcastability ends inside quantum theory and does not by itself certify nonclassicality. | Active |
| [THEORY-720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) | Cover-changing simulations add no contextuality | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md), Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5, read in [NOTE-651](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-651.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md), Theorems 21 and 22, read in [NOTE-647](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-647.md). A classical simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Non-contextual models are exactly those the empty model simulates, NCF cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and a model clones itself only if it is non-contextual. No-signalling models on finite scenarios only. Which maps are simulations is [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)'s open half. | Active |
| [THEORY-721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-721.md) | †-Frobenius algebras are orthonormal bases | Three results [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) rested on, held apart from its synthesis. (a) The unitary group acts transitively on the orthonormal bases of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and on its tensor factorisations of given dimensions, so neither is fixed by the space; a non-degenerate self-adjoint operator fixes a basis up to phases, and its invariant content is its spectrum. (b) Over ℂ, commutative special †-Frobenius algebras correspond exactly to orthonormal bases: Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary, [LIT-274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-274.md), Thm 5.1 and §6, in finite dimension; Abramsky & Heunen, [LIT-275](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-275.md), Thm 22, for the non-unital ones satisfying the H*-axiom, in any dimension. (c) Over ℝ it fails: ℂ as a real algebra, with multiplication scaled by 1/√2, is a commutative special †-Frobenius algebra with no nonzero copyable vector. | Active |
| [THEORY-807](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-807.md) | Concept combination has a quantum emergent layer | Aerts's reading, which [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 018) to the impossibility Theorem 9 proves. Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), read in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md), fits the ∆-type deviations with one emergent subspace per pair and reads thought as two superposed layers. The narrowing was right that the theorem does not force an emergent concept, only dropping the meet or the monotone weight; this entry is the emergence reading as Aerts's thesis. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1053.md) v2 | Repeatable records require orthogonal states | Zurek (2009), [LIT-1640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1640.md), eq. (5), read in [NOTE-1229](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1229.md). From \|u⟩\|e₀⟩ → \|u⟩\|e_u⟩ and \|v⟩\|e₀⟩ → \|v⟩\|e_v⟩, preservation of the scalar product gives ⟨u\|v⟩ = ⟨u\|v⟩⟨e_u\|e_v⟩, so either the record is no record or ⟨u\|v⟩ = 0. Zurek reads this as the origin of the outcome set of the collapse postulate. It does not give single outcomes, probabilities or which orthogonal set is chosen; that is the interaction's. | Active |
| [THEORY-1055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1055.md) | Redundant pointer records mark objectivity | Zurek (2009), [LIT-1640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1640.md), section II and Figs. 2–3, read in [NOTE-1229](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1229.md). Redundancy R_δ = 1/f_δ, the number of disjoint fragments each holding (1 − δ)H_S of the information about S, is large for states made by decoherence and absent for random states, and peaks sharply at the pointer observable. Those are model results the review cites. The step from redundancy to objectivity ("Large redundancy implies objectivity") is an identification. The later caveat, that mutual information alone does not guarantee independently accessible records, is not in the paper. Proposed for that step. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1058.md) | One prohibition yields quantum-like information | Deutsch & Marletto (2015), [LIT-1663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1663.md), §§7–8, read in [NOTE-1219](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1219.md). Active as a conditional. The derivations are informal but complete arguments from principles II–IX, and each feature is shown in the paper's own terms with no probabilities. The principles themselves are conjectures. It does not say that superinformation singles out quantum theory, or that the quantum features are derived from anything not already assumed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1066.md) v2 | Information defined without distinguishability | Deutsch & Marletto (2015), [LIT-1663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1663.md), §§3–5, read in [NOTE-1219](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1219.md). Active as a fact about the construction: the definitions are given in that order, and the base they give the recursion of (1.1) is checkable on the page. It does not say that these notions are the intuitive ones, which the authors disclaim, nor that the principles built on them hold. Its "intrinsic" excludes reference to a specific other substrate, not to generic ones, which the cloning task and (5.1) both use. | Active |
| [THEORY-1068](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1068.md) v2 | RQM's relata precede the relations | Rovelli (1996), [LIT-1635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1635.md), read in arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1227](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1227.md), §§II.C, III.A–B, III.D and IV.A. Active as a textual fact about the paper. It bears out, for 1996, what [THEORY-1071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1071.md) takes from Faye and Jaksland, who quote later texts for it. It does not say that RQM must keep systems prior, nor that the systems are uniquely given: the decomposition is assumed, not argued, and allowed to vary. | Active |
| [THEORY-1069](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1069.md) v2 | Measurement information grows continuously | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2025), [LIT-1676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1676.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1214](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1214.md), §VII and App. B. Active as mathematics: (B7) follows from (B6), which I rederived; (B8) as printed has a sign error, and the correct form is I_A^max − cos²(ωt)H_A. The continuity is of the expected quantities. A conditional relative fact appears at once in the ideal model, and the full-rank case that would remove that is described, not computed. The authors say the point is not specifically quantum. | Active |
| [THEORY-1071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1071.md) v2 | Quantum mechanics doesn't entail agential realism | Faye & Jaksland (2021), [LIT-1672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1672.md), read in [NOTE-1220](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1220.md), §5. Active: the non-entailment follows from the existence of an empirically equivalent interpretation with a different metaphysics, and the authors do not promote that interpretation. It does not say agential realism is inconsistent with quantum mechanics; that is [THEORY-1091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1091.md), a separate and weaker argument. | Active |
| [THEORY-1074](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1074.md) v3 | Perspectives merge by coupling, in examples only | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2025), [LIT-1676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1676.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1214](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1214.md), §VI and Apps. D–E. The merge, and the disturbance of a third party's relative fact, are computed in a three-system example and in Wigner's friend. The general claims, a solution to RQM's combination problem and consistency of perspectives, are asserted, not shown; whether they hold is THEORY-1213, Proposed. Every computation is relative to one outside system, where agreement is automatic. This is the same gap [THEORY-621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-621.md) and [THEORY-1080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1080.md) name. | Active |
| [THEORY-1075](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1075.md) v2 | Relative facts are only approximately stable | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2021), [LIT-1666](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1666.md), read in [NOTE-1226](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1226.md), §1 (pp. 2–6). Active: the definitions are the paper's, and the result follows in a few lines from a partial trace (eqs. 5–8) under two stated conditions, ε small and the third system not interacting with the environment. It does not say that stable facts are absolute, that decoherence settles which outcome occurred, or what fixes the division into systems. | Active |
| [THEORY-1076](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1076.md) v2 | Bohr doesn't support agential realism | Faye & Jaksland (2021), [LIT-1672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1672.md), read in [NOTE-1220](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1220.md), from Bohr's writings and the secondary literature. Active as exegesis: Bohr's own definitions of "phenomenon" (1938, 1949) and the convergence of realist and antirealist readings that Bohr never denied atomic objects. The dualisms half is interpretive and weaker. It does not say that Barad's view is false, only that it is not Bohr's. | Active |
| [THEORY-1078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1078.md) v2 | Possibility needs no actual constructor | Deutsch & Marletto (2015), [LIT-1663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1663.md), §§1–2 and footnote 1, read in [NOTE-1219](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1219.md). Active as a reading of the paper's definitions, which are explicit. It bears on A11's remark that constructor theory "could sharpen" what the record means by "a constraint being real", and it splits that notion. A possibility is a fact about the laws, which no particular thing realizes; a constructor is realized, approximate and deteriorating. It does not say that the framework's basic principle I is true, nor that a law of possibility is, or is not, a constraint realized by something ([CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1080.md) v2 | No observer's view is deducible from another's | Rovelli (1996), [LIT-1635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1635.md), read in arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1227](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1227.md), §§II.D, III.D, IV.A–B. The first half (no deducible relation between views, no in-toto description) is Rovelli's stated position, well supported by his text. The second half reports that consistency is shown for one case (von Neumann's correlation, p. 9) and left to the reader in general (p. 15); whether it holds in general is THEORY-1222, Proposed. Rovelli's own relativity analogy breaks where relativity supplies an invariant, which bears on [QUESTION-021](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-021.md) by analogy only. | Active |
| [THEORY-1081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1081.md) v3 | FR paradox misuses unstable relative facts | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2021), [LIT-1666](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1666.md), read in [NOTE-1226](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1226.md), §2 (pp. 7–11). The translation of Frauchiger and Renner's assumption (C) and of Bong et al.'s absoluteness of observed events into the use of eq. (3) across contexts is the paper's and is clear. That nothing else goes wrong is cited to others, inter-observer agreement is one sentence, and an agent reasoning about himself is left undone. What the paper argues is held; whether relative facts cohere in general is THEORY-1230's question. | Active |
| [THEORY-1091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1091.md) | Agential realism can't answer measurement problem | Faye & Jaksland (2021), [LIT-1672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1672.md), read in [NOTE-1220](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1220.md), §5. Proposed: the authors present it as a challenge ("There might be other more subtle ways"), and conclude only that consistency with quantum mechanics is unshown ("a leap of faith"), not that agential realism is incoherent. The exchange of 2026-10-27 reported it as "an unresolved measurement problem", which is the strength the text supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1093.md) v2 | Perspectives belong to commutative subalgebras | Di Biagio and Rovelli (2025), [LIT-1676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1676.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1214](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1214.md), §§II–V and IX. Active as a statement of the paper's definitions and of what follows from them: eq. (7) is an identity, and the restriction to commuting variables follows from the existence of joint distributions. It does not say that this resolves the problems the authors list, that observers play no role in fixing what counts as a fact, or that the choice of subalgebra is given by the physics. | Active |
